question: In which of the following buildings/towns constructed by the Mughals is Salim Chishti's tomb situated?
solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Salim Chishti’s tomb** is located in Fatehpur Sikri, Uttar Pradesh, India.
 
• Fatehpur Sikri was built by **Mughal Emperor Akbar** in the late 16th century and served as his capital for a short period.
 
• The tomb honors **Sheikh Salim Chishti**, a revered Sufi saint whose blessings were believed to have led to the birth of Akbar's son, Jahangir.
 
• Salim Chishti’s tomb is an exquisite example of **Mughal architecture**, featuring intricate marble work and a highly decorative design.
 
• The tomb is located within the sacred complex of the **Jama Masjid** in Fatehpur Sikri and is considered a significant pilgrimage site.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fatehpur Sikri:**

 
 
• Built between 1571 and 1585, Fatehpur Sikri is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• The city features several architectural marvels, including the Buland Darwaza, Jama Masjid, and Panch Mahal.
 
• It was abandoned due to water scarcity but remains an iconic representation of Mughal grandeur.
 
 
 
• **Sheikh Salim Chishti:**
 
 
• He was a 16th-century Sufi saint of the Chishti order.
 
• Akbar sought his blessings for a male heir, leading to the birth of Jahangir.
 
• His tomb is a revered site attracting pilgrims from across the globe.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Architecture:**
 
 
• Mughal architecture is characterized by symmetrical designs, intricate carvings, and use of red sandstone and marble.
 
• Key features include domes, arches, minarets, and large courtyards.
 
• Prominent examples include the Taj Mahal, Red Fort, and Fatehpur Sikri.
 
 
 
• **Jama Masjid in Fatehpur Sikri:**
 
 
• One of the largest mosques in India, built by Akbar in 1571.
 
• It serves as a central structure within the Fatehpur Sikri complex.
 
• Its design integrates Persian and Indian architectural styles.
